passage: The corporate VPN client reconnects automatically when the tunnel drops. If disconnects happen more than once an hour, switch from the UDP transport to TCP in the client's settings and restart the app. Persistent drops on home Wi-Fi are often caused by router-level packet filtering, so try a different network before opening a ticket.

Remote access starts with the corporate VPN client, which is preinstalled on all managed laptops. Sign in with your SSO credentials and complete the MFA prompt. First-time users should run the client once while on the office network so it can fetch the right configuration profile.

The default configuration is full tunnel: all traffic goes through the corporate VPN while it is connected. Split tunnel profiles exist for engineering teams that need direct access to vendor endpoints. Ask in the IT help channel for the profile name and it will be pushed to your device.

The VPN client may be installed on one personal machine per employee for light use such as checking dashboards. Personal devices must run a supported OS version and have disk encryption enabled before the client will connect. Heavy work should stay on your managed laptop.

Contractors receive a restricted VPN profile that reaches only the systems named in their statement of work. The profile expires after 90 days and is renewed by their internal sponsor. Contractors cannot reach the general file shares or the admin tools.

Video calls running through the full tunnel can lose quality on long-distance routes. The media endpoints are excluded from the tunnel on managed devices, so calls should connect directly. If you still hear stutter, set the client region to the one closest to you and restart it.

When the client hangs at the authenticating step, check that the system clock is set to automatic, then sign out of the client and back in. An expired MFA enrollment shows the same symptom. Re-enroll from the account portal if the clock is not the cause.
Staging is reachable over the VPN only. Connect, then use the staging dashboard URL from the internal wiki. Production access still requires a separate approval, and the VPN alone does not grant it.

When you replace your phone, enroll the new device in MFA from the account portal before deleting the old app. The VPN client picks up the new enrollment on the next sign-in. If you already wiped the old device, ask IT to send a fresh enrollment link.

Linux is supported through the command-line client in the internal package repository. The graphical client is not shipped for Linux. Connect with vpnctl up, and the configuration file lives in the .config folder of your home directory.

Passwords expire every 180 days and a reminder email arrives two weeks ahead. Change yours from the account portal; the new password cannot match the last five. If it already expired, the change must be done from the office network or over the VPN.

A sign-in loop in the CRM usually means the SSO session cookie was blocked. Allow third-party cookies for the SSO domain, or open the CRM in a normal window instead of a private one. Clearing cookies for just the SSO domain fixes it without signing you out everywhere.

A YubiKey that stopped being recognized can be re-paired from the account portal under security keys. Remove the old entry, plug the key into a USB port, and tap it when the browser prompts. Two keys are recommended so a lost one does not lock you out.

Missing MFA pushes are usually the notification permission on the phone, not the service. Open the authenticator app, force a token refresh, and check that battery optimization is not stopping it in the background. You can always type the six-digit code instead of approving the push.

Team credentials belong in the company password manager, in the team vault, never in a spreadsheet or a wiki page. Vault entries support notes, attachments and per-member access. Request a new vault through the account portal if your team does not have one.

Five failed sign-ins lock an account for 15 minutes as an anti-brute-force measure. The lock clears itself; there is nothing to reset. If you still cannot sign in after the lock clears, use the self-service recovery flow before contacting IT.

The company password manager has browser extensions for the four common browsers. Sign in to the extension with SSO; autofill then works on all sites except ones flagged as sensitive, where you copy from the app instead. Extension updates ship through the normal browser store.

External collaborators get scoped SSO accounts that expire with the project. They sign in with their own company email through a guest flow and see only the shared drives named in the invitation. Internal sponsors are responsible for removing access when the work ends.

One-time recovery codes are generated in the account portal under MFA settings, right after enrollment. Each code works once, and there are ten. Store them in the password manager, not in a note on the phone, because the phone is the thing you might lose.

Work accounts sign in only through the company SSO page. Sign-in buttons from big personal providers will not match your work identity and create a personal account nobody can administer. Always use the sign-in-with-SSO link, which the SSO portal lists per vendor.

Monitors up to 34 inches ship from the hardware catalogue with next-day delivery to the office. Choose the 27-inch model unless your work involves large spreadsheets or design. Home delivery is available once per employee per year.

Laptops are refreshed on a four-year cycle and the replacement request opens automatically 60 days before your refresh date. Early replacement needs manager approval and a reason such as hardware failure or a new role. Check your refresh date in the asset portal.

Broken peripherals are replaced without approval through the hardware catalogue; keyboards, mice and headsets all count. Submit the request and keep the broken item, IT sends a return label within a week. Next-day delivery applies to office addresses.

Docking stations come in two models: USB-C for current laptops and a legacy dock for the few remaining older machines. The catalogue picks the right one based on your assigned asset. One dock per person, home delivery included.

The mobile allowance covers part of a personal phone plan, paid monthly with salary. Submit the plan's first page as proof and the allowance starts with the next payroll cycle. The company does not own or manage personal phones, so no management software is installed.

Hardware repairs go through the office front desk: hand in the laptop in a padded sleeve with a short note about the fault. Repairs take three to five working days, and a loaner laptop is available on request. Data is not backed up for you, so sync before handing it in.

A second computer is approved only for roles that legally require device separation, such as some contractor work. Request it through the asset portal with a one-line justification. It is provisioned with the same image and counts as a separate asset.

The catalogue lists two approved headsets: a wired USB-C model and a Bluetooth one with a dongle. Both are tested with the meeting software and ship with spare ear pads. Choose Bluetooth only if you take calls away from the desk.

All company hardware is returned on or before the last working day; the offboarding checklist lists your items. IT sends a prepaid return box to your home if you work remotely. Unreturned items are charged against the final payslip where local law allows.

Left-handed input devices are stocked in the office supply room and in the hardware catalogue. The catalogue models have swappable button mappings configured by a small utility that IT preinstalls. Ask the office manager for the supply-room code.

Expense reports are due by the fifth working day of the following month. Reports submitted late are still paid, but roll into the next payroll cycle. The finance calendar on the intranet shows the exact dates for each month.

Client meals are reimbursable up to 60 per external guest, with one guest list required. Alcohol is covered up to a third of the total. Attach the itemised receipt, not the card slip, and name every attendee in the notes field.

Taxis and rideshares to airports are covered for business trips, including the early-morning and late-night ones. Choose the standard service class; premium tiers are reimbursed only when documented accessibility or equipment needs apply. Add the trip to your travel report, not a separate one.

A missing receipt is replaced by a signed declaration in the expense tool, which your manager countersigns. The declaration flow is capped at five percent of your monthly total. Card statements are not accepted as receipts.

Offsite accommodation is booked by the travel team within a set cap per city; Berlin sits at 140 per night. Personal upgrades to better rooms are paid privately. If you extend a stay for leisure, the extra nights and the room-rate difference are yours.

Private car use for business is reimbursed per kilometre at the rate published by finance each January. Enter the route in the mileage tool, which pulls the distance from the map. Fuel, parking and tolls on top are separate line items with their own receipts.

Flights under six hours are economy; long-haul flights over six hours can be booked in premium economy. Business class requires documented medical reasons and HR sign-off. Book through the travel tool so the fare lands in the right cost centre.

Approved expenses are paid with the second salary run after approval, so the typical wait is three to five weeks. The expense tool shows the planned payment date for each report. Rejected lines show a reason and can be corrected and resubmitted.

Team meals to mark a project milestone are covered from the team budget, up to 25 per person per quarter. The organiser submits one report with the attendee list. Regular weekly team lunches are not covered.

Policy flags in the expense tool are automatic and sometimes wrong. Add a comment on the flagged line explaining the context; finance reviews it within two working days. Do not delete and re-enter the line, that resets the review queue.

Report a lost badge in the access portal so it is blocked immediately, then pick up a new one at the front desk. A replacement costs nothing the first time. Badges found later must be handed back; they are re-issued, not reused.

The lab floor uses badge access; there is no door code. Lab access is granted to the teams working there and to visitors escorted by them. If your badge does not open the lab door, ask your manager to request the entitlement.

Guests are registered in the visitor system by the inviting employee at least one day ahead. The guest gets an email with a QR pass and Wi-Fi details. Reception prints the badge, and the host meets the guest in the lobby.

The building is open to badge holders on weekends from 9 to 19, with the main entrance closed and the side entrance staffed. No guest access on weekends. The gym and the roof terrace keep their own hours, posted at each door.

The basement bike room holds 80 bikes and opens with your badge, so registration is automatic. The room has charge points for e-bikes and a small repair stand with basic tools. Broken locks are replaced by facilities within a day.

A badge that suddenly fails at the turnstile is usually deactivated for inactivity after 60 days away, or it is due for renewal. Front desk staff can reactivate it in a minute with your laptop present. If reactivation fails, a new badge is printed on the spot.

Nobody lets you in: outside staffed hours the doors only open with your own badge, and tailgating counts as a security incident. If your badge does not work after hours, the access portal shows your entitlements. Weekend and evening access needs no special permission, just a valid badge.

New badges are printed on the morning of the first day and wait at the front desk. The manager gets a message when it is ready. Contractors receive time-limited badges that stop working on the contract end date.

Family visits are welcome in the lobby cafe and the ground-floor lounge, no registration needed. Deeper floors need a registered guest pass and an escort. Children under 14 must be accompanied at all times.

Parking is allocated by the transport portal in order of requests, with carpool and accessible spots prioritised. A spot is per person, not per car, and is valid for six months. Waiting times are posted on the portal home page.

Client-call rooms have soundproofing and a camera for four to six people; they are tagged client-ready in the room panel. Book through the calendar app by picking a room when you invite the client's dial-in. Keep the first and last 10 minutes free for setup and clear-up.

Rooms unclaimed 10 minutes into the slot release automatically and the panel shows free. This applies to every bookable room. If you join late, re-book from the panel rather than walking into someone else's meeting.

Recurring events are created once in the calendar app with the repeat rule set, not copied week by week. Pick the working-hours timezone so daylight saving does not move it. Rooms are found for the whole series when a room with enough capacity is free.

The two large rooms run the meeting software on the room computer; bring your own laptop and join as a participant for screen sharing. The ceiling microphone covers up to 14 seats. The touch panel starts the call with one tap on the listed meeting.

The booking system prevents new double bookings, but old holds can overlap after a schedule change. The room panel shows who holds the slot; message the holder to sort it out. Facilities resolves disputes in favour of client-facing meetings.
Four single-seat focus pods sit on floor 3 next to the library, bookable for up to three hours a day. No calls in the library itself. The pods have a small screen you can mirror to from your laptop.

Working hours in the calendar app come from your profile in the HR system. Fix the hours there and the calendar picks it up overnight. Meetings booked outside your hours are flagged to the organiser, not blocked.

External guests join through the meeting link with the lobby gate enabled, which keeps them in a waiting room until a host lets them in. Add their guest email, not their personal one. Recording stops automatically when an external guest joins a standup-type meeting.

Cancelling a series keeps single-occasion edits: moved or re-titled occurrences stay on calendars until cancelled one by one. The calendar app asks whether to notify edited occurrences. Choose yes, or people show up to an empty room.

Room capacity numbers on the door panels are fire-code limits, not suggestions. Panels refuse bookings above capacity for the room type. Larger events go to the events team, who open the foldable wall in the atrium.

Full-time employees have 28 paid vacation days per calendar year, prorated for the start year. Up to five unused days roll into the first quarter of the next year. Part-time balances scale with the contract.

Time off is requested in the HR portal; there is no minimum lead time, but two weeks' notice for a full week away keeps teams happy. Managers approve or reply within three working days. Approved days show in the team calendar automatically.

A doctor's note is required from the third day of illness onward; days one and two are self-certified. Send the note to People Ops, not to your manager. For longer illnesses, HR contacts you about a return-to-work plan.

Each office follows its own public-holiday calendar, published on the intranet in December for the next year. Your home office calendar applies to you, even if your team sits elsewhere. Days that fall on a weekend are not moved.

Parental leave starts with a conversation with People Ops at least eight weeks before the expected date. The portal has the paperwork, and statutory rules of your country override anything in the handbook. Returning parents can phase back in at 60 to 80 percent for up to three months.

Employees with four or more years of tenure can apply for a four to twelve week paid sabbatical. Applications go to the department head with a one-page plan, twice a year. Sabbaticals do not consume vacation days.

Workations from another country are allowed up to 30 days a year inside country list A, and up to 10 days in list B for tax reasons. Request it in the HR portal at least two weeks ahead. The two caps do not add up; the stricter one wins per country list.

Vacation days expire on 31 March of the following year, except the five that roll over. The HR portal shows your balance and the number that will expire. Managers can approve an extension for people on leave during the first quarter.

Unpaid leave from two weeks to three months is possible for personal projects or travel. Approval needs your manager and People Ops, and benefits pause for the duration. Vacation days are used up first where the reason allows it.

The office closes between Christmas and New Year; those days are company holidays and do not touch your vacation balance. Support rosters cover a skeleton crew, and slots are voluntary with a day off in return. The intranet lists the exact dates each year.

Payslips are in the payroll portal under Documents on the second working day of the month. They stay available for the whole employment plus ten years. A contact form in the portal reaches payroll for corrections.

Bank details are changed in the payroll portal up to the 15th of the month to apply that month. Changes entered later apply to the following month. Payroll never asks for bank details by email or chat.

The three health plans differ in deductible and dental cover; the comparison table is on the benefits page. Open enrollment runs each November, and changes outside it need a qualifying life event. The plan brochure lists which vaccinations are covered without deductible.

The company matches pension contributions up to 4 percent of base salary into the group scheme. The match vests after two years. You can change your contribution rate once a quarter in the payroll portal.

The annual tax statement is generated in late January and lands in the payroll portal under Documents. It shows total pay, tax and social contributions of the previous year. Paper copies are not sent by default.

Salary reviews happen once a year in the spring cycle; managers submit proposals in March and changes apply with the May payroll. Mid-cycle adjustments are possible after a role change. Budgets are set per department, not per person.

The transit subsidy covers 50 percent of a monthly public-transport pass, applied as a taxable benefit. Upload the pass receipt in the benefits portal once and it renews until you cancel. Bike schemes are separate and run through the leasing partner.

Bonuses earned in a year are paid with the March payroll of the following year. The target and the achievement percentage are visible in the performance tool before the payout. New joiners get a prorated target for their first year.

Statutory parental pay is topped up by the company to 100 percent of base salary for six months, per the parental policy. The top-up applies while the parental-leave agreement is active. Part-time phases scale the top-up with the contracted hours.

Overtime is logged in the time tool and either paid out or converted to time off, chosen per entry. Non-exempt roles are paid monthly with the salary; exempt roles take time off instead. Managers see the running balance in their team report.

Emails that ask you to open invoices or change bank details are the classic fraud pattern. Check the sender's actual address, not the display name, and report it with the phish button in the mail client. Never reply to ask if it is real.

The phish button sits in the ribbon of the mail client under the shield icon. On mobile it is in the three-dot menu of an open email. Reporting moves the mail to the security team and deletes it from your inbox in one step.

Report a lost device immediately in the security portal or by phone to the number on the badge; the device is wiped on next connection. Local police reports are needed for insurance within 48 hours. The travel insurance card in the wallet app has the emergency line.

Found USB sticks are handed to the security team, never plugged into a work machine. The security lab has an offline machine for checking them. If you already plugged one in, report it; there is no penalty for honesty, only for hiding it.

Passwords in tickets, chat or screenshots are a reportable incident even when accidental. The security team rotates the credential and scrubs the ticket. Nothing happens to you; hiding it is what causes harm.

The annual security training is due by the end of March and takes about 40 minutes. Reminders go out weekly during the last month. Unfinished training pauses access to production systems, not to your email.

Browser extensions need review before installation on managed devices; request it in the security portal with a link. Extensions that ask for mail or clipboard access are rarely approved. Personal browser profiles on work machines follow the same rule.

IT never asks for passwords, MFA codes or a remote session you did not request. Hang up and call the service desk on the number from the intranet. Phone-based pretexting is reported like phishing, with the same form.

Suspected data breaches go to the security on-call within the hour; the number is on the intranet front page. Do not delete evidence and do not email the affected files around. The security team runs the rest, including any notifications.

Requests to move money that arrive by email are fraud until proven otherwise, even with the right name and signature. Finance confirms every transfer through a second channel on a known number. Forward suspicious requests to the security team with the phish button.

Software not in the self-service catalogue is requested in the license portal with a one-line reason. Approved installs appear in the company software centre within a day. Local admin rights are not granted for manual installs.

Adobe seats are pooled per department and assigned in the license portal. Design holds twelve seats; unassigned seats release after 60 days of inactivity. Request a seat through your manager if the pool is empty.

The office suite is licensed per user, not per machine, so it installs on your laptop and one home machine. Sign in with your work account to activate. Deactivate an old device from the account portal when you hit the limit.

New vendors go through the procurement flow: a short form in the license portal, then security and legal review. Budget approval sits with your department head. The average review takes two weeks; rush reviews cost a rush fee.

License warnings at startup mean the machine has not talked to the license server in a while. Connect to the VPN and open the app once; the warning clears. Persistent warnings on a specific app go to the license portal's support chat.

Open-source tools may be used under their licenses as long as the license does not force the company to release code. The approved list is in the engineering handbook. Anything with an unusual copyleft clause needs a legal look before it ships in a product.

The chat tool supports scheduled notification pauses set from your profile; focus slots sync from the calendar. Emergencies break through the quiet state via the paging tool, not the chat tool. Your status shows a quiet badge to colleagues while paused.

New teams start in the company project tool; workspace creation is self-service from the tool's home page. Templates for sprints, campaigns and support queues load with one click. Guests from other departments join with their own accounts, no new license needed.

Video editing seats sit with the social team's pool in the license portal. The render farm queue is open to all teams with an approved project code. Editing on personal machines is not allowed because of the media-handling policy.

Beta and pre-release software runs only on the two lab machines reserved for it, not on daily-use laptops. Request lab access in the license portal. Bugs found there are reported to the vendor through the standard channel.

Short personal use of the VPN from holiday locations is fine and shows up in the usual logs, not in any alert. Keep it to reading and mail; large downloads from a residential connection trigger a low-priority review. The client works with the same profile abroad, no special travel setup is needed.

Public Wi-Fi is safe to use only through the VPN; connect the tunnel before opening anything that signs in. The client holds back sign-in traffic on open networks until the tunnel is up. Airports and hotels sometimes block VPN ports, and switching the transport to TCP gets around most of it.

Exporting the company vault is disabled; the encrypted sync across your own devices is the backup. If you need a copy for a migration, file a ticket and the vault admin exports it to a secured transfer. Never keep vault exports on the desktop.

The HR portal accepts only work accounts through SSO; a personal email at the same provider fails silently. Sign out of any personal sessions in that browser, then use the sign-in-with-SSO link. Bookmark the portal from the intranet to avoid lookalike pages.

Travel chargers are loaned from the IT cupboard for trips and returned on your first day back. The catalogue no longer sells chargers because the USB-C models are interchangeable. Ask the office manager for the cupboard code and log the loan in the asset portal.

Monitor arms are in the catalogue under desk accessories and fit the standard desk tops. Install them yourself with the included clamp; no facilities request is needed. Arms and the upgraded stands are not combined, pick one.

Visa fees and mandatory travel insurance for business trips are reimbursable as trip costs. Add them as separate lines in the travel report with their receipts. Fees for personal side trips are not covered, so split the receipt if the trip is mixed.

Small tips for hotel and restaurant staff are reimbursable up to about 10 percent of the bill; a cash receipt with a note works. Enter one line per hotel in the expense tool, not one per tip. Excessive tipping is flagged by the policy check like any other line.

The gym door accepts the normal employee badge; there is no separate gym pass. If the reader rejects your badge while the turnstiles work, the entitlement needs a refresh at the front desk. Day passes for partners are sold at reception.

Dogs are welcome on the last Friday of each month, with a pet entry in the visitor system. Owners keep dogs on their own floor and in the lobby cafe. Allergies take precedence; the office team mediates conflicts.

The medium rooms have wireless presentation only; there are no projectors left in the building. Bring a USB-C dock if your machine is older, the panel accepts HDMI through a dock. Cables are borrowed from the alcove shelves and returned the same day.

Rooms above 20 seats are the atrium and the workshop room on floor 1, and both are booked through the events team. Send date, headcount and setup to the events channel at least a week ahead. The foldable wall lets the atrium open into one big space.

A public holiday inside your vacation week is not charged to your balance; the portal subtracts working days only. No extra day is granted for weekends or holidays inside a vacation. The per-day subtraction is visible in the request preview before you submit.

Special paid leave covers your own wedding (two days), the wedding of a child (one day) and moving house (one day), per the special-leave table. Request it in the HR portal under special leave, adding the date as proof later. Special leave does not touch vacation or sick balances.

Child benefits run through the state; the company adds nothing on top. The payroll portal shows the tax class relevant to benefits, which you can change yourself. Questions about state payments go to the family office listed on the benefits page.

Wrong overtime entries are corrected by payroll within one cycle; open a correction request in the payroll portal with the affected month. Your manager confirms the logged hours in the same flow. Do not edit the time tool retroactively yourself.

Wearables that unlock or badge into doors are not approved; the readers ignore them, and the access policy says door tokens must stay company-issued. Use your badge. Smartwatches may stay connected to the mail app for reading, not for approving.

Client handoffs on USB use the encrypted-drive pool from the security cupboard; the drives unlock with a password shared on a second channel. Personal or unencrypted sticks must not hold client data. Log the handoff in the security register linked from the cupboard.

Both R and Python are free and preinstalled on managed machines through the internal package mirror. Paid add-ons with point-and-click interfaces need the normal license portal request. The data team wiki lists the recommended setup per role.

The approved writing assistant runs inside the docs tool with client data excluded by policy. Generic public chatbots must not receive client documents. The approved list of assistants is maintained on the security page under tool review.

Guest Wi-Fi vouchers for visitors staying in the workshop flat next to the office are ordered from reception. The voucher covers one device for a week, and the flat network is separate from the office guest network.

The travel router in the loan kit connects to hotel networks and links back to the office over the VPN automatically. It exists for trips where the hotel blocks VPN ports; book it from the asset portal like any other kit.
Roaming data plans are reimbursed up to 30 per trip when a local SIM is cheaper than roaming. Keep the VPN on regardless of which network the laptop uses.
Personal vault entries stay private to you; the admin cannot read them even for recovery. If you lose access to your personal space, recovery runs through your recovery codes, not through IT.
The benefits portal and the HR portal share the SSO session. If you switch between them and get bounced, open each from the intranet links rather than saved bookmarks.
Charging cabinets with 20 USB-C bays sit in each kitchen for phones and tablets during the day. They are not for laptops; the bays deliver 20 watts only.
The desk tops are 160 by 80 with a cable channel down the middle. Clamps for arms and dividers fit the channel; glue and screws into the top are not allowed.
Conference tickets are booked by the travel team together with flights when the event is approved. Early-bird deadlines are not a reason to book privately; late fees are the team budget's problem.

Room service and the minibar are personal costs even on business trips, with breakfast the exception when the room rate includes it. The hotel bill must be itemised to split covered from private lines.
The bouldering wall in the event hall opens on Thursdays with the sports club. Climbing shoes are loaned at the door, and the wall is off limits outside club hours.
The office cat policy is that there is no office cat; the two cats sometimes seen in the courtyard belong to the corner cafe.
The presentation clickers live in a basket in each medium room; take one per session and return it to the basket, not to your desk. Clickers pair with the room computer automatically.
The events team maintains a stock of flipcharts, pinboards and moderator cases. Kits are wheeled to your room on request; book at least a day ahead.
Bridge days are regular vacation days used to connect a public holiday to a weekend. They are requested like any vacation and follow the same notice convention.
Bereavement leave is granted for close family, three days within the country and five with travel, per the special-leave table. People Ops arranges the details privately.
The company kindergarten places are allocated each spring through the benefits portal, and waiting lists are visible to everyone. The sibling rule gives preference when one child already attends.
Payslip lines are documented in the payroll wiki: each deduction code links to the page that explains it. The overtime code OT1 differs from the time-off-in-lieu code, which shows as TIL.
The contactless lunch card is separate from your badge and works in the canteen only. It cannot open doors, and losing it costs nothing; report it in the canteen app for a same-day replacement.
Downloads from the file-share links are logged and expire after 30 days. The log is visible to the share owner and to the security team on request.
The statistics sandbox machines in the lab run the heavier data tools on request; they are for one-off jobs that would melt a laptop, not for daily work. Jobs queue through the lab portal.
MFA reminder: the six-digit code window is 30 seconds. If your code keeps failing, the phone clock drifts; enable automatic time in the phone settings.
The VPN connection counts as one of your two allowed devices. Swapping a device releases the old slot automatically after 14 days.
Lost hardware is not charged to you if the loss is reported within two working days. Report it in the asset portal; silent losses count as unreturned equipment.
Meals during overtime after 19:00 are covered as a flat 12, submitted as one line per evening in the expense tool. Receipts are not needed for the flat rate.
The visitor parking spots P1 to P4 are booked in the transport portal by the host. They are for guests with mobility needs or heavy samples, not for daily commuting.
Standup agendas live in the recurring event description; edit it before the meeting starts, not the single occurrence description.
Desk plants are watered every two weeks by the office team. If yours looks thirsty before then, the watering can lives next to the printer alcove on each floor.
The second-floor printer handles A3 and staples automatically. Large jobs above 50 pages should go to the copy room machine, which is faster and rarely jams.
Visitor Wi-Fi runs on a separate network with a 4 Mbps cap per device. If a guest needs more, the IT help channel can raise the cap for 24 hours.
The office library lends books on an honour system for up to four weeks. Returns go on the shelf marked returns, not back in the alphabetical sections.
Standing desks adjust with the paddle under the right side; hold it to lower. The counter stores the saved heights for two users.
First aid kits hang in every kitchen at eye level next to the fire plan. The names of current first aiders are listed on the kitchen notice board.
The emergency assembly point is the small park across the street from the main entrance. Roll calls are taken by floor wardens, who wear yellow vests during drills.
Paper and small electronics are shredded on the first Wednesday of each month in the courtyard. Batteries go to the red box in the lobby, not to the shredding pile.
The coffee machines descale themselves overnight on a schedule. If a machine still tastes off, put an out-of-order note on it and mail the office team.
Mailing lists are created by the IT help channel on request. Open lists accept mail from any employee; closed lists need the owner to approve senders.
The intranet search indexes wiki pages, portal entries and policy PDFs. It does not index the ticket system, so older resolutions are invisible to it.
Meeting etiquette asks that one person types notes into the event description so absent colleagues can read back. Recordings are opt-in, not default.
Remote work chairs are subsidised once every three years through the ergonomic equipment form. The subsidy covers up to 300 from the partner shop.
The support phone rota lives in the team calendar; the current week's owner answers the number printed on the intranet front page.
Offsite planning has a checklist template in the wiki: venue, travel, budget line, and a weather plan for outdoor parts. The travel team books within the city caps.
Ergonomic assessments take 45 minutes and are offered every quarter. Sign up in the benefits portal; the assessor leaves adjustment tips in a short PDF.
Showers are on floor 2 next to the bike room, with towel service on weekdays. Weekend users should bring their own towel.
Lost property ends up in a box at the front desk and is donated at the end of each quarter. Valuables like phones go to the security team instead.
The printer alcoves stock notepads, envelopes and a few USB-C cables. Everything else is ordered through the office supplies form.
Kitchen fridges are cleared every Friday at 16:00. Containers without a name sticker go to the shared shelf, which is fair game.
The all-hands runs on the first Tuesday of the month with a recorded version posted by Wednesday. Questions go into the anonymous form linked in the invite.
Roof terrace furniture is stored in the box during winter. The terrace reopens with the first week above 15 degrees, announced in the office channel.
Fire drills happen twice a year without warning. The record time to clear the building is four minutes, set in the spring drill of 2024.
The travel team holds a monthly surgery for trip questions in the help hub. Walk in with your booking reference for changes the tool cannot make.
